agentProfiles.name: frontier
agentProfiles.notes: Frontier-class hosted models with rich harness tooling. Owns architecture, control-plane, multi-module slices.

agentProfiles.name: mid
agentProfiles.notes: Mid-tier capabilities — single-agent tool use without subagent dispatch. Owns bounded slices within one module. May run cloud (Sonnet, GPT-4o-mini) or local (Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen-2.5-72B in LM Studio/Ollama).

agentProfiles.name: small
agentProfiles.notes: Local-small tier (16K context floor). NOT a slice owner — runs as deterministic helper for header sync, README generation, commit-message templating, prettier-fix, doc-translation, narrow extracts. Always invoked by a higher-tier agent that owns the slice.

notes: .claude/CLAUDE.md is the Claude adapter to the shared contract.
Claude-specific subagents, hooks, and detailed skills remain supported but do not redefine the shared delivery process.
AGENTS.md is the Codex adapter to the shared contract.
Codex-compatible skills are generated into .agents/skills/ from the canonical contract.
.cursorrules is the Cursor adapter to the shared contract.
Generated by scripts/agent-contract/sync.mjs — do not edit manually.

local.firstAction: Before any other action, run `node scripts/agent-context.mjs --slice=$SLICE_ID --files=<comma-separated paths>` to receive a token-budgeted brief sized to your tier (`--profile=small` for ≤16K context, `--profile=mid` for default, `--profile=frontier` for ≥64K). Read the brief top to bottom; deep-read only the Touched files section.
notes: LOCAL.md is the slim adapter for any harness driving a mid- or small-tier agent.
MICRO.md is an ultra-slim adapter for narrow helper tasks where even LOCAL.md is too much budget.
Generated by scripts/agent-contract/sync.mjs in the TPL-209 slice (not yet); this entry reserves the slot.
MICRO.md intentionally omits the briefer call — deterministic helpers do not own slices and do not need context briefing.

principles: Prefer the smallest implementation-ready slice that can be proven locally.
Before implementing any user-facing behavior change, use product-planner first and confirm persona/workflow USM plus PRD coverage exists.
Keep commits atomic and reviewable; one slice should become one commit before the next slice begins.
Never mark work complete before checks, acceptance proof, changelog discipline, and commit discipline are satisfied.
Use deterministic repository scripts and hooks as the executable truth.
Keep architectural boundaries explicit and avoid broad repo wandering.
Treat trunk plus Branch by Abstraction as the default delivery model.
Never git add -u or git add . — always name specific files. Scope repo-wide fix scripts (header-fix, readme-fix, prettier, eslint) to your active directory, not repo-wide.
deliveryFlow: Route structural or orchestration changes through repo-architect.
Use product-planner first for new intake, decomposition, USM, or PRD routing.
For user-facing behavior work, stop implementation until persona/workflow USM and PRD coverage are real and linked.
Use designer for user-facing design or prompt-authoring work when needed.
Update traceability artifacts before or alongside the first implementation slice.
Write the smallest proving test first.
Before modifying files outside your target module, check .claims/ for active claims and file your own claim (ADR 0008).
Implement one bounded slice through feature-implementer or frontend-specialist.
Close acceptance through acceptance-tester before finalization.
Commit the bounded slice before starting the next slice.
Sync headers, READMEs, and generated adapters.
Run architecture, delivery, control-plane, compatibility, pre-implementation, USM, test, and changelog gates.
Create artifacts only when a snapshot or zip is actually needed.
testGate: Bugfixes start from a failing regression test.
UI or UX changes require Gherkin coverage.
Visible browser proof should be runnable in headed mode when debugging or validating user-facing flow changes.
The test gate is not green until deterministic repo checks and the shipped fast-path proof layers pass.
bddConventions: One .feature file per module or per user flow — never a monolithic all-features file.
Each .feature + its step definitions must fit within a 4K-8K token file-size budget (keeps test files small and modular).
Each Scenario is fully independent — no shared mutable state, no ordering dependencies between scenarios.
Scenarios describe user-visible behavior in domain language, not implementation mechanics.
Selectors in Playwright-backed BDD come from the bounded ui-selectors registry, never hardcoded in step definitions or feature files.
Test data uses builders or factory helpers, not hardcoded fixture objects that couple to model shape.
Cross-module scenarios are forbidden in tests/bdd/ — one scenario proves one module's behavior.
When a module is detached, its .feature file and step definitions detach cleanly with it.

A dedicated cross-module walkthrough under tests/e2e/ is exempt from the one-module-per-feature rule — it intentionally chains flows across modules in a single headed browser session for visual end-to-end verification.
acceptanceFlow: Acceptance closes the implemented slice against linked backlog and spec intent.
Add only the smallest missing proof needed to decide readiness.
A slice is not ready for finalization until acceptance proof is explicit.
Ready-for-finalization does not mean done until the bounded slice is committed.
changelogFlow: Keep CHANGELOG.md current for commit-ready work.
Use deterministic changelog sync rather than ad-hoc manual drift.
Changelog notes must stay bounded to the current slice instead of batching several slices together.
commitFlow: Commit only after repo gates and acceptance are green.
Use conventional commit shape with at least one work-item ID.
One slice equals one commit; do not accumulate multiple completed slices before committing.
Large batched changesets must be resliced or justified explicitly.
finalizationFlow: Do not treat a task as complete until checks, changelog, and commit discipline are satisfied.
Use mergezip or test:all:mergezip only when release artifacts are needed.
Keep unfinished behavior behind a stable seam or flag until proof is green.
Do not move to the next slice while the current slice is still uncommitted.
doneDefinition: Trace links resolve for the changed slice.
The changed implementation/proof files reference a ready work item through SpecRefs.
Required tests and deterministic checks pass.
Architecture and public-API boundaries still hold.
Headers, READMEs, and generated adapters are aligned.
CHANGELOG.md and commit discipline are satisfied.

roles.name: repo-architect
roles.useWhen: structural, orchestration, control-plane, or seam design work
roles.notes: No localTierEquivalent — choosing module boundaries, naming public APIs, and shaping seams is reasoning that no deterministic script can substitute for. If small-tier work points here, escalate.

roles.name: product-planner
roles.useWhen: new intake, decomposition, backlog normalization, or mandatory PRD/USM routing before implementation
roles.notes: No localTierEquivalent — authoring PRD/USM and decomposing intake into ready slices is reasoning. The pre-impl-gate.mjs / usm-check.mjs scripts only verify whether that reasoning has already happened; they do not produce it.

roles.name: designer
roles.useWhen: user-facing visual language, prompt templates, accepted assets, or design handoff
roles.notes: No localTierEquivalent — visual language, prompt authoring, and asset acceptance are creative judgments. The design-docs-check.mjs script only validates folder structure, not design quality.

roles.name: feature-implementer
roles.useWhen: bounded implementation slices outside heavy UI concerns
roles.notes: No localTierEquivalent — implementing behavior, choosing test shape, and reading collaborator files is the reasoning core of the role. A small-tier agent should not own this.

roles.name: frontend-specialist
roles.useWhen: visible UI, accessibility, messages/i18n, or selector discipline matters
roles.notes: No localTierEquivalent — UI delivery requires component composition, a11y judgment, and selector design. No deterministic script substitutes for it.

roles.name: acceptance-tester
roles.useWhen: closing acceptance or deciding finalization readiness

localTierEquivalent.scope: Run the deterministic test gate that proves the changed slice still passes the project's required tests.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Cannot decide WHICH proof to add for a missing acceptance criterion, and cannot judge ready-for-finalization — those require slice-level reasoning. Stop and escalate when the gate passes but acceptance criteria are not yet covered.

roles.name: control-plane-supervisor
roles.useWhen: cross-surface drift or orchestration consistency is in doubt

localTierEquivalent.scope: Detect drift across canonical instructions, hooks, scripts, docs, and adapters.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Detection only. Repairing the canonical owner (deciding which file is the source of truth and rewriting it) is reasoning the small-tier agent should not perform — surface findings and escalate.

roles.name: release-operator
roles.useWhen: artifact packaging or release/finalization discipline is needed

localTierEquivalent.scope: Run the full atomic commit ceremony — pull, claim enforcement, VERSION bump, CHANGELOG release, commit, claim auto-complete, snapshot.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Requires staged slice files and a --message="<type>(<scope>): <summary> (TPL-XXX)" argument prepared by the caller. Does not author the slice or its CHANGELOG bullet — those must already exist under [Unreleased].

skills.name: acceptance-validation
skills.purpose: Close an implemented slice against acceptance and determine readiness for finalization.
skills.whenToUse: When the code exists and acceptance proof is the missing step.
steps: Compare slice behavior against linked backlog/spec intent.
Add only the smallest missing proof.
Decide ready-for-finalization only when acceptance is explicit.
Do not mark the slice done until commit discipline is also satisfied.
Verify BDD .feature files are scoped to one module or flow, not monolithic.
Verify scenarios are independent with no shared mutable state or ordering dependencies.
Verify selectors come from the ui-selectors registry, not hardcoded strings.
Reject cross-module scenarios in tests/bdd/ — the dedicated walkthrough under tests/e2e/ is exempt.

localTierEquivalent.scope: Run the deterministic test gate to prove the slice does not regress existing coverage.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Does not author the missing proof and does not decide ready-for-finalization. Surface gate output and stop — adding the smallest missing proof is mid-tier reasoning work.

skills.name: bdd-playwright
skills.purpose: Express visible behavior through Gherkin and deterministic browser-oriented proof when needed.
skills.whenToUse: For UI or UX changes that need Gherkin coverage or browser smoke proof.
steps: Write or tighten Gherkin scenarios first.
Map selectors through the bounded registry and stable hooks.
Keep browser proof deterministic and scoped to the visible change.
Use headed mode when you need to watch the user-facing flow directly.
Keep each .feature file scoped to one module or one user flow — never a monolithic all-features file.
Ensure each .feature + step definitions fit within a 4K-8K token file-size budget.
Use domain language in scenarios, not implementation details.
Cross-module walkthroughs belong in tests/e2e/ only — tests/bdd/ stays modular.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — authoring Gherkin scenarios in domain language and binding them to selectors requires UI-shape reasoning. The pnpm test:bdd command only re-runs existing scenarios; it does not write new ones.

skills.name: changelog-release
skills.purpose: Keep changelog and release/finalization discipline aligned with the real change.
skills.whenToUse: Before commit-ready finalization or artifact generation.
steps: Sync CHANGELOG.md structurally.
Confirm artifact creation is actually needed.
Keep release notes aligned with the bounded slice.

localTierEquivalent.scope: Move existing [Unreleased] bullets into a versioned section stamped with VERSION + today's date. Idempotent on empty [Unreleased] (skips with no error).
localTierEquivalent.limits: Does not author CHANGELOG bullets — the slice's Added/Changed/Fixed/Removed entries must already exist under [Unreleased] before this runs. coa-merge invokes this internally; prefer that over running release.mjs by hand.

skills.name: control-plane-audit
skills.purpose: Audit drift across instructions, hooks, scripts, docs, and tests, then repair the real source.
skills.whenToUse: When orchestration surfaces or agent adapters may have diverged.
steps: Run deterministic drift checks first.
Classify disagreement as source drift, unsupported claim, or stale adapter.
Fix the canonical owner instead of layering duplicate prose.

localTierEquivalent.scope: Detect drift across canonical instructions, hooks, scripts, docs, and adapters.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Detection only. Classifying findings and repairing the canonical owner is reasoning. Surface findings and stop.

skills.name: control-plane-design
skills.purpose: Shape repo-level orchestration and control-plane changes without creating duplicate authority.
skills.whenToUse: For new process surfaces, role maps, or compatibility-layer design.
steps: Choose a canonical owner first.
Keep adapters thin and explicit.
Back new orchestration claims with scripts, hooks, or tests.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — choosing canonical owners and shaping new orchestration surfaces is reasoning. The check.mjs script only verifies an existing design, it does not produce one.

skills.name: design-delivery
skills.purpose: Carry user-facing design work from intent to accepted handoff without replacing PRD or USM.
skills.whenToUse: For brand, screen-state, prompt-authoring, or asset-handoff work.
steps: Keep design docs under docs/design/.
Use design as a supplement to PRD and USM.
Hand off only accepted assets or explicit references.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — design intent, prompt authoring, and asset acceptance are creative judgments. design-docs-check.mjs only validates folder structure.

skills.name: feature-delivery
skills.purpose: Implement one bounded backlog slice by deep-reading only touched files and direct collaborators.
skills.whenToUse: For implementation-ready changes that should stay small and locally understandable.
steps: Start from one implementation-ready backlog slice.
Stop and route back through product-planner if the slice lacks mandatory PRD or USM coverage.
Read deeply only what you will change.
Commit the slice before moving on to the next one.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — implementing a slice requires reading collaborators and writing code. The pre-impl-gate.mjs script only verifies the slice's USM/PRD coverage exists; it does not deliver the slice.

skills.name: frontend-delivery
skills.purpose: Implement visible UI slices with explicit accessibility, messages, and selector discipline.
skills.whenToUse: For user-visible UI work or DOM-contract changes.
steps: Keep copy in a messages layer from day one.
Use stable selectors from a bounded registry.
Treat accessibility states as part of the slice, not a follow-up.
Do not start user-facing implementation until persona/workflow USM plus PRD coverage exists.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — UI delivery requires component composition, a11y judgment, and selector design. No script substitutes for it.

skills.name: header-sidecar
skills.purpose: Keep structured headers and sidecars aligned with the real file role.
skills.whenToUse: When files are added or their responsibility changes.
steps: Use inline headers where safe.
Use <file>.header.md sidecars for comment-sensitive formats.
Repair semantic drift at the header owner, not in random comments.

localTierEquivalent.scope: Regenerate or repair sidecars and stamp version/date for files in the current diff.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Cannot decide which files need new headers from scratch — use header-create.mjs explicitly for that. Cannot repair semantic drift in @purpose lines without operator review.

skills.name: hex-boundary
skills.purpose: Preserve modular boundaries and public-API-only access across the repo.
skills.whenToUse: When a change touches module boundaries or imports.
steps: Go through public APIs only.
Avoid deep imports and hidden cross-module reach-through.
Escalate to repo-architect when the existing seam is insufficient.

localTierEquivalent.scope: Detect deep imports and public-API-only violations across modules.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Detection only. Repairing a violation by carving a new public-API surface or seam is repo-architect work — surface findings and escalate when the existing seam is insufficient.

skills.name: prd-usm-backlog
skills.purpose: Normalize intake, PRD, USM, and backlog so implementation slices start from the right source.
skills.whenToUse: For new requests, decomposition, or spec normalization.
steps: Record raw intake first.
Use product-planner first for decomposition and readiness checks.
Use USM first for user-facing workflow changes.
Advance only implementation-ready slices into execution.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — authoring PRD, USM, and slicing intake into ready backlog items is reasoning. usm-check.mjs / product-docs-check.mjs only validate that the reasoning has happened.

skills.name: readme-discipline
skills.purpose: Keep folder-level READMEs aligned with real ownership and entrypoints.
skills.whenToUse: When folder purpose or workflow entrypoints change.
steps: Update the owning folder map.
Keep the README navigational instead of policy-duplicating.
Make real entrypoints discoverable.

localTierEquivalent.scope: Create missing READMEs and align folder-level navigational content with discovered entrypoints.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Cannot decide whether a folder is meaningful enough to need a README in the first place — that decision belongs to the slice owner. Operates on currently tracked folders only.

skills.name: repo-nav
skills.purpose: Navigate untouched repo areas through headers, public APIs, tests, and nearby docs first.
skills.whenToUse: When you need context without loading large parts of the codebase.
steps: Start from headers and folder docs.
Use public APIs and tests as the next boundary.
Only deep-read internals when the current slice truly depends on them.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — navigation through headers, public APIs, and tests is a reading strategy, not a script. control-plane-check.mjs is referenced for drift verification, not navigation.

skills.name: security-audit
skills.purpose: Screen risky commands, sensitive paths, and security regressions before calling work done.
skills.whenToUse: When changes touch permissions, secrets, dangerous commands, or sensitive areas.
steps: Respect the portable dangerous-command blocker.
Keep secrets out of docs and headers.
Escalate security-sensitive ambiguity instead of guessing.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — security audit requires reasoning about secrets, dangerous patterns, and policy. Running one regression test does not constitute an audit.

skills.name: spec-traceability
skills.purpose: Keep backlog, PRD, USM, design, and proof references aligned around the changed slice.
skills.whenToUse: When behavior, scope, or acceptance changes.
steps: Update linked docs and IDs.
Repair stale references before finalization.
Keep traceability tight enough for acceptance review.

localTierEquivalent.scope: Verify that PRD, USM, backlog, and proof references resolve consistently for the changed slice.
localTierEquivalent.limits: Detection only. Repairing a stale reference (deciding which doc to edit and how) is reasoning — surface findings and stop.

skills.name: tdd
skills.purpose: Start from the smallest failing proof, then implement only what makes it pass.
skills.whenToUse: By default for implementation and especially for bugfixes.
steps: Write the failing proof first.
Implement the smallest change that makes it pass.
Keep refactors separate from proof creation when possible.
Prefer finishing and committing the proven slice before opening the next failing proof.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — authoring the failing proof and the matching implementation is the heart of the skill. test-gate.mjs only re-runs existing tests; it cannot write a new one.

skills.name: trunk-bba
skills.purpose: Ship through trunk using Branch by Abstraction and stable seams instead of long-lived hidden branches.
skills.whenToUse: When new behavior cannot replace the old path in one safe slice.
steps: Introduce the seam first.
Keep new behavior disabled by default until proof is green.
Land seam-first or slice-first commits atomically rather than batching multiple finished slices.
Remove the old path later in its own atomic cleanup when clearer.
skills.notes: No localTierEquivalent — choosing where to introduce a seam, when to keep the old path, and when to remove it is reasoning. The named scripts only verify trunk delivery discipline once decisions exist.

enforcedRules.rule: Tests must not write to git repositories outside os.tmpdir() / RUNNER_TEMP
Worktrees are ephemeral; audit + safe cleanup primitives required
Every commit lands on trunk OR on a tx-<slice> transport branch; ceremony bumps gated by a coa-merge marker; ff-update to trunk is repo-shape-aware (F12)

branches.update-ref-bare: bare repo (core.bare=true AND --is-bare-repository=true) — keep R2 baseline update-ref
branches.update-ref-no-main: non-bare with no main worktree — update-ref + stderr warning
branches.push-update-instead: non-bare with main checked out elsewhere AND receive.denyCurrentBranch=updateInstead — git push --force-with-lease against the main worktree path
branches.refuse-needs-config: non-bare with main checked out elsewhere but config not set — refuse with operator-actionable one-time setup command

mainWorktreeSync.rationale: F12 (TPL-237) — original update-ref left main worktree desync'd when main checked out elsewhere; updateInstead atomically advances ref AND syncs the working tree, refusing on dirty destination by built-in semantics. Auto-configure is intentionally NOT the default so we don't silently mutate the destination repo's config.

auditMatrix.notes: Root process adapter for each tool.
Codex gets role routing through AGENTS and skills; Cursor uses a single flat rules file.
Shared process summary is generated from one skill map.

auditMatrix.codexArtifact: shared repo scripts and git hooks
auditMatrix.cursorArtifact: shared repo scripts and git hooks

All tools rely on the same deterministic commands and proofs.
